callback window validity is decided by the dialogue model from code-computed window facts (not code)
identity flow (which question, re-asks, declines) follows the dialogue model with the bank's verification results

extra rule (stateful, stage opening): Ask for identity confirmation at most twice; non-confirming replies such as 'hello', 'go ahead' or 'who is this' trigger the second ask; if it is still unclear after the second ask, close not_reached/unclear. Answering a customer question first does not reset the count. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (stateful, stage identity): Track total wrong identity answers across both questions; on the third, end the check, do not state the debt, point to the mobile app or a branch, and close not_verified/failed. A day_month_swapped retry and an unreadable value are not counted. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (stateful, stage identity): On the first refusal to answer the security questions (or the first question about the call's purpose instead of an answer), explain once that the questions protect the account; on the second, close not_verified/declined. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (stateful, stage global): Count 'do not want to talk' statements; on the second, close no_promise/refused after verification or not_verified/declined before it. - left to the dialogue model's prompt
extra rule (stateful, stage global): On a request for a human, ask once whether you can help first; transfer to general only if they insist. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (stateful, stage third_party): When a third party offers a callback time outside the window, ask once for another time; if that is also outside, close not_reached/no_callback without scheduling. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (stateful, stage negotiate): Count persuasion attempts per the band (1 early, 2 late). Only flat refusals, non-answers, refusal of the deadline after a later date, and refusal of an offered floor use an attempt; a customer-proposed date or amount never does. When attempts are used up, close no_promise/refused without repeating a refused offer. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (stateful, stage negotiate): Offer the floor at most once after 'too much' and at most once after a below-floor amount; remember whether the customer said the full amount is too much, so that attempt 1 uses the floor. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (stateful, stage negotiate): Hardship (illness, death in the family, job loss) takes precedence over persuasion and restructuring: one sentence of sympathy, no persuasion attempt, offer a support transfer; if declined, close no_promise/hardship. A date or amount the customer names themselves is still recorded. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (computational, stage negotiate): Resolve the customer's 'next <weekday>' as that weekday in the following calendar week and 'this <weekday>' as the one in the current week, relative to now, before the date check. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (stateful, stage negotiate): A confirmation is bound to the exact product, amount and date read back; any change invalidates it and requires a new check and readback. - left to the dialogue model's prompt
